selection: Selected evidence-rich manufacturers, developers and project operators; not exhaustive or a market-share ranking. Private control not inferred from named investors.

records.name: LONGi
records.ownership: Public, Shanghai 601012. June 2026 filing identifies Li Zhenguo and Li Xiyan as actual controllers, together holding 19.105%.
records.funding: Equipment sales, operating cash and debt; disclosed CNY2.4bn technology-innovation green bond in its 2025 results. These finance the company, not every customer solar farm.
records.evidence: Reports 86.58 GW of module shipments in 2025; 22.87 GW of back-contact module sales. Shipments are factory output, not installed AC generating capacity.
records.cost: No company-specific electricity price assigned. Solar benchmark: US$44/MWh global 2025 commissioned projects; module selling price excludes installation and finance.
records.demand: Already supplies equipment at tens of GW per year. Higher efficiency can lower land and installation needs per watt.
records.limitations: Industry losses and price competition can weaken warranties and expansion even when solar technology is sound.
records.geopolitics: Chinese supply chains, import restrictions and local-content rules change delivered prices; company reports adapting its US supply chain.
records.next_evidence: Financial health, warranty provision, factory yields and delivered project prices.

records.name: First Solar
records.ownership: Public, Nasdaq FSLR; owned by public shareholders. A controlling shareholder was not established in this review.
records.funding: 2025 filing reports US$5.2bn revenue and US$2.4bn net cash; manufacturing tax credits support margins. Customer sales and corporate finance support factories.
records.evidence: Commercial cadmium-telluride modules. Reports 17.5 GW sold in 2025.
records.cost: Use the same solar plant benchmark as LONGi, not the manufacturer’s revenue divided by shipped watts as electricity cost.
records.demand: A large non-silicon supply route for utility solar. Factory sales do not specify when customer plants connect.
records.limitations: Manufacturing execution, material supply, module performance and customer project delivery.
records.geopolitics: US manufacturing incentives and tariffs affect its competitive position; diversification can reduce dependence on crystalline-silicon supply chains.
records.next_evidence: Comparable site-specific output, installed cost, contracted delivery and policy sensitivity.

records.name: Oxford PV
records.ownership: Private UK/German company. Board represents strategic and financial investors; current percentages and control were not verified.
records.funding: Historical £65m 2019 financing involved Goldwind, Equinor, Legal & General and Meyer Burger. This is a dated event, not a current cap table or cash balance.
records.evidence: Reported first commercial shipment of perovskite-silicon modules in September 2024.
records.cost: No independently established commercial fleet electricity cost found; do not apply a laboratory efficiency record as a cost reduction.
records.demand: More electricity from constrained roof or land area; eventual contribution sits inside solar, not on top of it.
records.limitations: Long outdoor life, moisture/heat tolerance, production yield, encapsulation and warranty backing.
records.geopolitics: European manufacturing and intellectual property may diversify supply; industrial scale still competes with large Asian manufacturers.
records.next_evidence: Multi-year full-size outdoor results, degradation guarantees and price per delivered lifetime kWh.

records.name: Vestas
records.ownership: Public, Nasdaq Copenhagen VWS. 2025 annual report states 100% free float and names BlackRock at 8.61% as notified July 2025; this is not majority control.
records.funding: Equipment and service revenue, corporate financing and customer orders; 2025 group revenue €18.822bn, rather than venture funding.
records.evidence: 201 GW cumulatively installed by end-2025; 14.537 GW delivered during 2025. Cumulative installations are not a current operating-fleet audit.
records.cost: Onshore benchmark US$33/MWh global 2025; offshore US$78/MWh. Neither is a Vestas quote.
records.demand: Existing production and service network supports substantial near-term expansion.
records.limitations: Permitting, grid connections, repairs, blade reliability, offshore factory ramp and installation vessels.
records.geopolitics: Trade barriers and local manufacturing requirements can change supplier eligibility and cost.
records.next_evidence: Annual deliveries, turbine availability, warranty costs and the customer’s final project budget.

records.name: Equinor / Hywind
records.ownership: Listed company; Norwegian state owns 67%. Hywind Tampen has several field partners; Equinor is not the sole project owner.
records.funding: Corporate and partner capital; government roadmap records NOK2.3bn Enova support for Hywind Tampen. This is historical project support.
records.evidence: Hywind Tampen fully operating since 2023; 11 turbines upgraded to 94.6 MW total turbine rating. Export infrastructure was not upgraded by the same amount.
records.cost: No current standardized floating-wind price established here. The US$78/MWh offshore benchmark must not be treated as a floating-wind quote.
records.demand: Accesses deep-water wind near coastal or offshore demand; output remains weather-dependent.
records.limitations: Moorings, dynamic cables, marine maintenance, ports and financing.
records.geopolitics: Norwegian industrial policy and oil-and-gas supply-chain expertise support deployment; procurement and seabed access vary by country.
records.next_evidence: Actual annual energy, maintenance expenditure and competitive repeat-project bids.

records.name: Westinghouse
records.ownership: Brookfield consortium owns 51%; Cameco owns 49%. Supplier ownership is separate from the utilities that own reactors.
records.funding: Parent equity and established fuel/service revenue; each new plant requires separate project finance and customer commitments.
records.evidence: Established reactor, fuel and service supplier. Operating AP1000 projects demonstrate the design; a new country still has construction risk.
records.cost: US Vogtle-based new nuclear benchmark US$175–255/MWh; IEA repeat-build country assumptions are lower. Neither is a universal vendor price.
records.demand: Large plants and lifetime support can supply dependable generation; construction and retirement rates determine expansion.
records.limitations: Financing during long builds, project management, local skills and nuclear-qualified components.
records.geopolitics: Export approvals, sovereign relationships and fuel diversification influence contracts and schedules.
records.next_evidence: Project-specific completed cost, schedule, financing and repeat-build performance.

records.name: EDF
records.ownership: French state sole shareholder following 2023 nationalization. Individual foreign projects have separate ownership arrangements.
records.funding: Utility cash flow, debt and state-backed industrial policy; government ownership is not unlimited free capital.
records.evidence: Large operating nuclear fleet. Filing reports Flamanville 3 connected in December 2024 and reached full nominal output in December 2025.
records.cost: Existing operations, life extensions and new EPR builds have different costs. No single EDF electricity cost assigned.
records.demand: Keeping productive plants operating and completing repeat builds both matter for supply.
records.limitations: Construction delays, refurbishment, component manufacturing, outages and cooling-water conditions.
records.geopolitics: French and UK nuclear policy, financing structures and cross-border industrial cooperation shape delivery.
records.next_evidence: Plant-level availability and completed costs; distinguish generation milestones from sustained annual output.

records.name: KHNP / KEPCO
records.ownership: KHNP is 100% owned by KEPCO in its end-2025 subsidiary disclosure. At Barakah, project and operating companies are ENEC 82%, KEPCO 18%.
records.funding: Utility group resources and customer/project finance. A reactor vendor and the plant’s equity owners are different entities.
records.evidence: Four APR1400 units at Barakah entered commercial operation between 2021 and September 2024: 5.6 GW nameplate total.
records.cost: No harmonized completed-project electricity cost established here. Avoid comparing an export construction contract with Vogtle’s full financed cost.
records.demand: Repeated large reactors provide an operating counterexample to treating all nuclear construction as a US project.
records.limitations: Local construction capability, financing, supplier capacity and country-specific licensing.
records.geopolitics: Bilateral nuclear agreements, export finance and technology/IP permissions affect accessible markets.
records.next_evidence: Comparable all-in costs and schedules for the next export project.

records.name: GE Vernova Hitachi / OPG
records.ownership: US venture: GE Vernova 60%, Hitachi 40%. Its Japanese sister venture has different ownership. OPG is the Darlington project owner, not the reactor vendor.
records.funding: Corporate development plus OPG’s project capital. First-unit C$7.7bn budget includes shared infrastructure, interest, contingency and escalation.
records.evidence: 300 MW BWRX-300 at Darlington is under construction; CNSC records construction authorization and a subsequent operating-license application.
records.cost: C$7.7bn / 300 MW ≈ C$25,700/kW with that broad first-unit boundary. It is not an overnight price or a repeat-unit forecast.
records.demand: If operated at an assumed 85% annual output, one 300 MW unit yields about 2.23 TWh/year.
records.limitations: First-build execution, licensing, manufacturing scale and finance; conventional light-water fuel avoids assuming every SMR needs HALEU.
records.geopolitics: Canadian procurement and US/Japanese supply chains support deployment; each new jurisdiction needs authorization.
records.next_evidence: First operating unit and subsequent-unit cost reductions with identical accounting.

records.name: TerraPower
records.ownership: Private developer founded by Bill Gates. Exact current voting control not established.
records.funding: June 2025 US$650m equity round included Gates, HD Hyundai and NVentures. DOE demonstration support is distinct from corporate equity.
records.evidence: NRC authorized construction permit issuance in March 2026; company announced nuclear plant construction in April. These are achieved milestones, not operating generation.
records.cost: No completed Natrium plant cost or verified electricity price yet.
records.demand: 345 MW design plus heat storage; temporary higher output from storage is not extra continuous reactor energy.
records.limitations: HALEU fuel, sodium systems, plant integration, licensing to operate and on-budget construction.
records.geopolitics: US nuclear policy and non-Russian enrichment capacity affect the schedule; international industrial investors can support manufacturing.
records.next_evidence: Fuel deliveries, construction progress, operating authorization and full plant cost.

records.name: X-energy
records.ownership: Public, Nasdaq XE following April 2026 IPO. Founder Kamal Ghaffarian and Amazon appear in financing/registration records; current voting percentages not asserted here.
records.funding: Q2 results report about US$1.1bn net IPO proceeds. Earlier US$700m Series C-1 was anchored by Amazon; customer agreements are not additional equity.
records.evidence: Xe-100 reactor and TRISO fuel development; no operating commercial Xe-100 fleet established in this review.
records.cost: No verified operating-fleet price; do not substitute a proposed SMR average for this design.
records.demand: Modules target electricity and industrial heat; planned deployments are conditional on licensing, fuel and construction.
records.limitations: Fuel production/qualification, first plant construction and project finance.
records.geopolitics: Domestic fuel policy, industrial heat customers and strategic computing buyers influence deployment.
records.next_evidence: Regulator milestones, fuel factory throughput and a completed customer plant.

records.name: Commonwealth Fusion Systems
records.ownership: Private company; full cap table and voting control not established.
records.funding: July 2026 company announcement reports US$1bn new equity, US$4bn cumulative. Google and Eni also have power-buying relationships.
records.evidence: SPARC is a fusion demonstration; ARC is a proposed power plant. Neither establishes sustained net commercial grid electricity.
records.cost: Commercial electricity cost unverified; fundraising and a power agreement do not establish a delivered price.
records.demand: ARC targets roughly 400 MW in the early 2030s. At assumed 85% output this would be 2.98 TWh/year, not current supply.
records.limitations: Net plant output, neutron damage, maintenance, tritium supply/breeding and plant construction.
records.geopolitics: National R&D support and specialized magnet/fuel supply chains matter; export partnerships can expand industrial capacity.
records.next_evidence: Independent net-electric performance, fuel balance, duty cycle and a complete plant budget.

records.name: Helion
records.ownership: Private company; exact control and investor percentages not verified.
records.funding: Series G announcement updated to US$500m closed in September 2026, led by Thrive Capital.
records.evidence: Orion target: at least 50 MW and initial operations in 2028. No independently verified commercial net-electric operating record established here.
records.cost: No verified commercial cost. A prospective power contract is not evidence of the cost of fulfilling it.
records.demand: 50 MW at an assumed 85% average output would produce 0.37 TWh/year. That availability is an assumption, not demonstrated performance.
records.limitations: Net electric gain, repetition rate, component survival, maintenance and fuel cycle.
records.geopolitics: Public R&D support and strategic power customers can accelerate development without removing technical risk.
records.next_evidence: Independent metered net output and sustained operation before relying on the deployment date.

records.name: Fervo
records.ownership: Public after May 2026 IPO. Current controlling voting interest not established in this review.
records.funding: Q2 filing reports US$2.2bn gross IPO proceeds and US$421m project debt for Cape Station’s first phase. Corporate equity and project debt fund different needs.
records.evidence: Company reports 33 MW net commercially operating at Cape Station on 1 October 2026; remaining first-phase units were still commissioning.
records.cost: No independently verified fleet-average EGS cost. Conventional geothermal’s US$89/MWh is a comparator, not a Fervo price.
records.demand: 33 MW at assumed 85% annual output is 0.246 TWh/year. Larger announced phases are future capacity.
records.limitations: Drilling cost, sustained reservoir flow/temperature, pumping, induced seismicity and repeatability.
records.geopolitics: Oilfield drilling skills and equipment transfer to geothermal; water and subsurface permitting remain local.
records.next_evidence: Multi-year net output, well decline, pumping load and repeated project construction costs.

records.name: Eavor
records.ownership: Private Canadian developer; exact voting ownership not verified. Disclosed investors include Canada Growth Fund, bp Ventures, Chubu, Temasek, OMV and Microsoft’s climate fund.
records.funding: June 2025 CGF commitment up to about C$138m: C$89m at financial close and about C$48m milestone-dependent; not all unconditional cash.
records.evidence: Geretsried first grid power reported December 2025. A March 2026 research-group visit confirms the first of four planned loops operating; economics still being evaluated.
records.cost: Commercial repeat-project cost unverified. Avoid treating planned full output as measured output from the first loop.
records.demand: Can supply heat and electricity without relying on natural reservoir permeability; useful heat and electric output must be accounted separately.
records.limitations: Drilling length/cost, heat transfer, thermal decline and site temperature.
records.geopolitics: Canadian capital and European project support help early builds; heat-network access can determine the customer market.
records.next_evidence: Annual net output, sustained heat extraction and full construction/operating cost.

records.name: Quaise
records.ownership: Private; Nabors disclosed 14% fully diluted ownership and largest-shareholder status in August 2026. This is not majority control.
records.funding: US$180m Series B final close includes Nabors’ US$35m investment; US$280m total funding reported. Do not add the US$35m twice.
records.evidence: Drilling and project development; no operating Quaise power plant verified. Millimeter-wave drilling and the whole geothermal plant are separate engineering tests.
records.cost: No demonstrated commercial electricity cost.
records.demand: Project Obsidian initial 50 MW target; later expansion is conditional. Deep heat resources are not a construction forecast.
records.limitations: Deep hot-hole drilling, casing/materials, well completion, reservoir management and net conversion performance.
records.geopolitics: Drilling-contractor partnership supports equipment and execution; site permitting and technology supply chains still matter.
records.next_evidence: Full-depth wells and sustained net power at known cost.

records.name: CATL
records.ownership: Public in Shenzhen and Hong Kong. End-2025 filing identifies Xiamen Ruiting, controlled by Zeng Yuqun, as controlling shareholder with 22.45%.
records.funding: Large sales/cash-generating manufacturing business and public capital; 2025 revenue RMB423.7bn. Not a venture-stage project.
records.evidence: 2025 lithium-ion sales 661 GWh across uses; this includes vehicle batteries and must not be called 661 GWh of grid storage.
records.cost: IRENA four-hour installed storage benchmark US$140/kWh in 2025. This is a system-level global benchmark, not CATL cell price.
records.demand: Daily shifting, fast grid response and backup. Storage consumes charging electricity and is not new primary generation.
records.limitations: Duration, degradation, efficiency, safety, grid connection and mineral supply.
records.geopolitics: Chinese manufacturing concentration, trade restrictions and localization rules affect customer access and cost. Sodium-ion can change material needs, but needs its own evidence.
records.next_evidence: Stationary-system delivered price, guaranteed cycles, installed capacity and usable energy.

records.name: Form Energy
records.ownership: Private company; full cap table and control not verified.
records.funding: August 2026 US$750m Series G led by T. Rowe Price; backers include Sequoia, Breakthrough Energy Ventures and GE Vernova.
records.evidence: Iron-air systems target 100-hour discharge. Great River Energy’s April 2026 filing awaited remaining Cambridge modules and expected operation by year-end; completed acceptance not verified here.
records.cost: Installed price and operating-fleet performance not independently established. Low material cost does not establish full system cost.
records.demand: Addresses multi-day shortfalls. The announced 80 GWh backlog is contracted storage energy, not operating GW or annual generation.
records.limitations: Round-trip losses, footprint, cycle life, manufacturing yield, recharge time and capacity-payment economics.
records.geopolitics: US manufacturing support and utility procurement help establish an early market.
records.next_evidence: Customer-confirmed commissioning, discharge tests, efficiency and complete installed cost.

records.name: Hydrostor
records.ownership: Private Canadian developer. Disclosed backers include Goldman Sachs Alternatives, Canada Growth Fund and CPP Investments; ownership percentages not established.
records.funding: Announced US$230m financing in August 2026. A separate 2025 announcement named US$200m investor financing; do not sum without reconciling instruments and overlap.
records.evidence: Goderich has operated since 2019: 1.75 MW discharge, more than 10 MWh physical storage, 7 MWh contracted.
records.cost: No verified repeat-project electricity delivery cost established; large proposed plants cannot inherit a pilot price.
records.demand: Long discharge and grid services; stores electricity rather than adding primary energy.
records.limitations: Cavern geology, civil works, compressors, efficiency, permits and project finance.
records.geopolitics: Canadian institutional capital and long-duration procurement in different markets help revenue certainty.
records.next_evidence: Completed large-scale construction cost, guaranteed usable energy and measured round-trip efficiency.

records.name: Rondo Energy
records.ownership: Private company; exact ownership percentages not verified.
records.funding: 2023 US$60m financing included Microsoft’s climate fund, Rio Tinto, Aramco Ventures, SABIC, SCG, TITAN, BEV and other investors. Historical round, not current cash.
records.evidence: Company reported a 100 MWh heat battery in commercial operation in October 2025, delivering industrial steam.
records.cost: No independently verified heat price here. Claimed >97% efficiency is electricity-to-heat, not electricity-to-electricity.
records.demand: Stores cheap electricity for industrial heat; can replace fuel use while increasing electricity demand.
records.limitations: Charging price/window, heat delivery temperature, customer process integration and full installation cost.
records.geopolitics: Industrial customers, electricity tariffs, carbon prices and domestic fuel prices determine competitiveness.
records.next_evidence: Metered heat, charging energy, availability and a delivered heat contract.

records.name: Panthalassa
records.ownership: Private public-benefit corporation; founder and investor identities do not establish voting control.
records.funding: May 2026 US$140m Series B led by Peter Thiel; announcement names John Doerr, TIME Ventures and industrial participants.
records.evidence: Wave-powered offshore computing concept with announced 2026 pilot and 2027 commercialization targets; commercial operating performance not independently verified.
records.cost: Need cost per useful compute task including hardware, communications, maintenance and losses. Grid electricity cost alone is the wrong product comparison.
records.demand: Could serve workloads suitable for offshore operation and data links; cannot directly supply every grid customer.
records.limitations: Storm survival, energy variability, salt/corrosion, computing utilization, heat removal, repair and communications.
records.geopolitics: Maritime jurisdiction, shipping/fisheries, data rules, chips and satellite access affect deployment.
records.next_evidence: Metered wave input/net power, useful compute output, uptime, repair cost and lifecycle economics.

records.name: CorPower Ocean
records.ownership: Private Swedish developer; current control/percentages not verified.
records.funding: €32m Series B1 in 2024 led by NordicNinja, SEB Greentech and EIT InnoEnergy. Separate EU grant and EIC equity pre-commitment support early arrays; commitments are not all received cash.
records.evidence: C4 demonstrated grid export in Portugal. Company schedule: 10 MW VianaWave investment decision in 2027, operations in 2029/30.
records.cost: No bankable CorPower fleet price established. IRENA’s early-wave estimate US$454/MWh is a sector reference, not this company’s bid.
records.demand: Potential coastal power and complementary weather patterns; seasonal/storm performance and local resource govern output.
records.limitations: Survival, device availability, maintenance vessels, arrays, cables and financing.
records.geopolitics: EU demonstration grants and regional industrial policy can fund learning before unsubsidized competitiveness.
records.next_evidence: Independent annual generation, availability, repair spend and array-level cost.

records.name: Orbital Marine Power
records.ownership: Private Scottish developer; exact current shareholder control not verified.
records.funding: O2 used EU/Scottish support and a £7m Abundance construction debenture. These are project funding records, not current equity valuation.
records.evidence: O2 is an operating 2 MW turbine. October 2026 EURO-TIDES announcement advances a four-turbine array targeting 2028, subject to investment completion.
records.cost: No verified commercial fleet price. Sector early-tidal estimate US$358/MWh is not an Orbital contract.
records.demand: Predictable local generation in strong currents; slack tides still require complementary supply.
records.limitations: Limited suitable channels, maintenance, cable access, marine ecology and scale economics.
records.geopolitics: UK price-support contracts and EU demonstrations create early demand; public procurement continuity matters.
records.next_evidence: Metered annual output, fleet maintenance and contracted costs for the next array.

records.name: Ampeak Energy / MeyGen
records.ownership: AIM-listed AMP, formerly SIMEC Atlantis Energy. February 2026 notification gives Patrick Hughes an indirect 29.6% interest through Landpad/SUEH. That is a dated substantial holding.
records.funding: Existing generation revenue, public-market finance and supported power contracts. Expansion still needs project finance; parent battery projects are separate.
records.evidence: MeyGen’s installed four-turbine array is 6 MW; servicing affects availability. Expansion awards for 59 MW are not an operating fleet.
records.cost: No harmonized completed-array electricity cost verified. A support contract price is revenue, not production cost.
records.demand: Operating-array evidence is valuable for learning; planned expansion is small relative to global demand.
records.limitations: Underwater repairs, availability, financing and repeating arrays at viable sites.
records.geopolitics: UK Contracts for Difference support early economics; ownership changes and finance affect delivery.
records.next_evidence: Annual output and maintenance record, and expansion financial close. Do not mistake cumulative GWh for one year of output.

records.name: Minesto
records.ownership: Public, Nasdaq First North. October 2026 financing notice identifies Corespring New Technology as largest shareholder; older percentage table is dated May 2025.
records.funding: October 21 notice proposes about SEK130m rights issue, dependent on later approvals; about 60% covered by undertakings/guarantee. Proposed proceeds are not cash received.
records.evidence: Company reports extended grid-connected Dragon tests in the Faroes, including the 1.2 MW Dragon 12. Demonstration is not an operating multi-unit commercial farm.
records.cost: Commercial fleet electricity cost not verified.
records.demand: Underwater kites seek to use lower-speed tidal sites, potentially expanding usable locations.
records.limitations: Tethers, control, marine servicing, annual availability and financing.
records.geopolitics: Island utilities and public demonstration support provide entry markets; local ecological and navigation permissions remain.
records.next_evidence: Independent annual energy, maintenance, repeat sales and completed equity financing.

records.name: Global OTEC
records.ownership: Privately held developer; current ownership/control not verified in reviewed sources.
records.funding: Named project support: September 2026 Bahamas study commissioned by Expertise France and financed by the EU. A study budget is not financing for a completed power plant.
records.evidence: Bahamas feasibility work and floating-platform development; no commercial Global OTEC electricity fleet established here.
records.cost: No current independently verified commercial price. Tropical diesel displacement is a relevant comparator, not the cheapest mainland solar alone.
records.demand: Potential continuous tropical power plus cooling/water services, if site and economics work.
records.limitations: Small temperature difference, pumping loads, heat exchangers, large deep-water pipe and storm survivability.
records.geopolitics: Island fuel-import dependence and development finance create demand; coastal jurisdiction and environmental consent affect projects.
records.next_evidence: Sustained net power after pumps, pipe reliability and separately priced electricity/water/cooling.

records.name: Sweetch Energy
records.ownership: Private French company; full cap table and voting rights not verified.
records.funding: €25m Series A in December 2023 led by Crédit Mutuel Impact’s fund; participants included CNR and EDF Pulse Ventures alongside existing financial investors.
records.evidence: OPUS-1 is an operating demonstrator in the Rhône delta. Company estimate of roughly 500 MW installable locally is potential, not its present plant output.
records.cost: No independently established commercial fleet price.
records.demand: Could use natural river/seawater salinity differences or some industrial streams; useful output is limited by site flow and net energy balance.
records.limitations: Membrane fouling/life, intake/filtration/pumping power, available freshwater and ecological constraints.
records.geopolitics: French utilities and public support help demonstration; water rights and drought influence site availability.
records.next_evidence: Net exported power after all water handling, membrane replacement costs and annual operation.

records.name: thyssenkrupp nucera / NEOM project
records.ownership: Listed nucera: thyssenkrupp 50.19%, De Nora 25.85%, Saudi PIF 6%, remainder free float. Customer NGHC is an equal ACWA/Air Products/NEOM venture.
records.funding: NGHC’s 2023 financial close: US$8.4bn project value and US$6.1bn non-recourse financing, with 30-year Air Products offtake. This is customer project finance, not nucera equity.
records.evidence: Large electrolyser deployment underway. Sponsor’s current page targets first product in 2027; do not reuse the old end-2026 operating target.
records.cost: Current ACWA project page lists US$9.046bn project cost, versus US$8.4bn financial close. Boundaries/reconciliation need checking; neither is a hydrogen unit price.
records.demand: Serves chemical/feedstock and fuel demand; electrolysis adds electricity demand. Returning hydrogen to electricity incurs further losses.
records.limitations: Low-cost clean power, electrolyser utilization, water, conversion/transport and customers willing to pay.
records.geopolitics: Saudi industrial strategy, export markets, clean-fuel certification and shipping routes affect delivery.
records.next_evidence: Commissioning, metered hydrogen yield, firm end customers and reconciled project cost.
